㊥ Gist: `gpt-6-luna` is refused, so the Codex reader is running on the default Codex model, `gpt-5.6-sol`. The chunk-3 packet now carries the Baldwin lesson.

㊩ (luna) I registered a new Codex seat, codex-9, with `gpt-6-luna`. Its first job failed at once. Codex answered: "The 'gpt-6-luna' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account." So luna needs an API account. Nothing reached the batch directory.

㊢ (what is running) I switched codex-9 to `gpt-5.6-sol`, which is the default in your Codex config, reset its session and sent chunk 3 again. It is running, and the session log shows sol.
- Job: `invoke-1790787937896-29242-fa5af79f`
- Park: `park-65f0013c-1185-4baf-9414-05bac66d9ccc`, 55-minute deadline
- The park on the failed luna job has already been cleared.

🈕 (what changed in the packet for chunk 3)
- **Two searches per fragment,** one for the move and one for the subject using the turn's own nouns. The packet cites the Baldwin miss as the reason.
- **Named families:** if the turn names a library family, the reader lists it and must cite or reject at least one of its patterns.
- **Later patterns:** a pattern created after the turn can be cited, with a note that the turn came first.
- **Glosses** for `explore`, `retract` and `withdraw`. A standing permission stays `approve` for now, with "standing permission" written in the rationale.
- **No overwriting:** the reader must not delete a published record and must stop and tell me instead.

㊟ (comparing readers) Chunk 3 is the first under the new rules, so it is not a like-for-like comparison with Zai and Sonnet on chunks 1 and 2. When it comes back I will report problems, citations and time per ten turns for all three. I will also report how often the family rule caught something.

🈯 (if you want luna or astra) The CLI's other model, `gpt-6-astra`, is the one your config note says burns usage, so I did not try it. If your reset token gives luna through an API key, I can register a second Codex seat on it and send it the next chunk.

previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: You are right, and I take back my acceptance of chunk 1. Its readers never looked at a single Baldwin pattern, and my measurements show the same fault across all earlier readings, the live ones included.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (my "the library may have little on them") That was wrong and I had not checked it. The library has 29 patterns that mention Baldwin, including a `baldwin/` family of 11. The reading of your Baldwin turn looked at three patterns and none of them was one of those.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why it happened) The readers search for the move and drop the subject. Their queries for that turn were "shift the work from running experiments to building the argument" and "point out that a pattern library for the concept is missing". Neither contains the word Baldwin. When I ran a query with the word in it, the search tool returned `baldwin/ARGUMENT`, `baldwin/two-claims-not-one` and `meta/baldwin-ratchet-defeats-darkroom` as its top three.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (how widespread it is) I counted turns that name a pattern family outright and where the reader read no pattern from that family:

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (a detail on that turn) Your turn says "there is no `futon3/library/baldwin/`". The family's first pattern was added the same day, and another on 14 August. So that turn is the origin of the family, which is a stronger relation than a citation. Two Baldwin patterns already existed at the time and were also unread: `futon-theory/baldwin-cycle` from February and `problems/baldwin-causal-claims-vs-engineering-metaphor` from March.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(changes to the reading instruction)
1. Two searches per fragment: one for the move and one for the subject, the latter using the turn's own nouns.
2. When the turn names a pattern family, the reader reads that family's patterns and cites or rejects them explicitly.
3. The checker fails a reading where a named family has no pattern read. I have that check written as `/tmp/claude17/subject_check.py`. Its wider form, which looks at any rare title word, is too noisy to use as a gate, and the family-name form is the usable one.
4. A pattern that did not exist when the turn was written can still be cited, with a note that the turn came first.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two decisions)
- Shall I apply changes 1 to 4 to the backfill packet and the live 象 instruction together? The live change raises the interpretation version.
- The 441 batch readings and 83 live ones that missed a named family could be reread for patterns only, keeping their segments and intents. Do you want that queued after the backfill, or before it?
